Rashi on Shabbat 16a:1:1.english: Natron - A type of white earth.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:1:2.hebrew: מיטמאין ומטמאין מאוירן - נתלית טומאה באוירן — נטמא מן האויר; חזר ותלה אוכלין באוירן — מטמאין את האוכלים. ואע"פ שלא נגעו — טמא, דכתיב: "כל אשר בתוכו יטמא", ואפי' מלא חרדל, שאין נוגע בדפנותיו אלא הסמוך לדפנות:
Rashi on Shabbat 16a:1:2.english: They become impure and render [other items] impure from their airspace - [If] a source of impurity was suspended in their airspace, [the vessel] became impure from the airspace; [if] one subsequently suspended food in their airspace, [the vessels] render the food impure. And even though they did not touch [the vessel], it is impure, as it is written: “Whatever is in it shall become impure” (Leviticus 11:33) — and even [if the vessel is] full of mustard [seed], where only that which is adjacent to the walls touches its walls.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:1:3.hebrew: ומיטמאין מאחוריהן - אם נכנס טומאה לתוך אחוריהן מבחוץ, במקום חקק בית מושבם, כדרך שעושין לכלי עץ:
Rashi on Shabbat 16a:1:3.english: And they become impure from behind - If impurity entered into their back from the outside, at the place of the indentation of their base, in the manner that they make for wooden vessels.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:1:4.english: And they do not become impure from their outer side - As it is written: “Into its interior.”

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:1:5.english: They have a remedy - To melt them down and remake them into vessels.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:2:1.hebrew: לטומאתן ישנה - אם נטמאו ונקבו וטהרו, וחזר ועשה מהן כלים — יחזרו לטומאתן להטעינן טבילה, הואיל וככלי מתכות נינהו:
Rashi on Shabbat 16a:2:1.english: To their previous impurity - If they became impure, and were perforated and [thereby] became pure, and he then remade vessels from them — they should return to their [previous] impurity, to require immersion for them, since they are like metal vessels.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:2:2.english: They became pure - For it is no [longer] a vessel.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:2:3.english: They reassume their previous impurity - Ahead, [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:2:4.hebrew: פשוטיהן טהורים - דאיתקש עץ ועור לשק, דיש לו בית קבול. וכלי עצם איתקש לעץ ועור בפרשת מדין (במדבר ל״א:כ׳), "כל בגד וכל כלי עור וגו'", ואמרי' בהכל שוחטין (חולין דף כה:): להביא דבר הבא מן העזים — מן הקרנים, ומן העצמות, ומן הטלפים. וכלי זכוכית — לקמן מפרש טעמא אמאי פשוטיהן טהורים, מאחר דדמו למתכות:
Rashi on Shabbat 16a:2:4.english: Their flat [vessels] are pure - For wood and leather are compared to sackcloth, which has a receptacle. And bone vessels were compared to wood and leather in the portion of Midian (Numbers 31:20): "Every garment and every leather vessel, etc."; and we say in [the chapter entitled] Hakol Shochetin (Chullin 25b): [This comes] to include anything that comes from goats — from the horns, and from the bones, and from the hooves. And [as for] glass vessels — later, [the Gemara] explains the reason why their flat [vessels] are pure, seeing that they resemble metal [vessels].

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:3:1.hebrew: וטומאה ישנה - שיחזרו לה מאחר שטהרו ממנה, דרבנן היא, כדלקמן בהילכתא:
Rashi on Shabbat 16a:3:1.english: And previous impurity - That [vessels] should return to it after they were purified from it is rabbinic, as [explained] below in the halakha.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:3:2.hebrew: בטומאת כלי מתכות דאורייתא - גזור טומאה ישנה, אבל בכלי זכוכית — דעיקר תחילת טומאתו ליתא אלא מדרבנן — לא גזרו טומאה ישנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 16a:3:2.english: With regard to the impurity of metal vessels, [which is] from the Torah - [The Sages] decreed previous impurity, but with regard to glass vessels — since the very origin of their impurity is only rabbinic — they did not decree previous impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:4:1.hebrew: פשוטיהן מיהא ליטמא - ככלי מתכות, דהא פשוטי כלי מתכות דאוריי'. וכיון דדכוותייהו שוינהו — ליטמא, דליכא לשנויי בהא כדשני' בטומא' ישנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 16a:4:1.english: Their flat [vessels] should in any case become impure - Like metal vessels, for flat metal vessels are [impure by] Torah law. And since [the Sages] equated them to them, they should become impure, for one cannot answer regarding this as we answered regarding previous impurity.

Rashi on Shabbat 16a:4:2.hebrew: עבדי רבנן הכירא - בטומאת כלי זכוכית, וחילקו בה מטומאה דאורייתא, להודיע שהיא מדבריהם, ולא ישרפו עליה תרומה וקדשים. דלא שרפי תרומה משום טומאה דרבנן, בר מן ו' ספיקות (לעיל שבת דף טו:):
Rashi on Shabbat 16a:4:2.english: The Sages made a distinction - In the impurity of glass vessels, and they differentiated it from impurity by Torah law to make known that it is of rabbinic origin, so that they would not burn *terumah* and consecrated items on account of it. For they do not burn *terumah* on account of rabbinic impurity, except for the six doubtful cases (above, Shabbat 15b).

Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:1:1.hebrew: לא ליטמאו מגבן אלמה תנן כלי נתר וכלי חרס כו' - וקשה לרשב"א, דהוה ליה לאתויי ברייתא דתוספתא דכלים: "מחט וטבעת ושולי כלי עץ, וכלי זכוכית, וכלי עצם — אין ממלאין בהן, ואין מקדשין בהן, ואין מצילין בצמיד פתיל", אלמא דמיטמאין מגבן! ואמאי מייתי הא, דלא מצי לאוכוחי מינה אלא על ידי דיוק: "כלי נתר וכלי חרס הוא דטומאתן שוה כו'"? ועוד, אהך דמייתי איכא למימר: דלא חשיב אלא כלי נתר וכלי חרס דהוו דאורייתא — דכלי נתר נפקא לן בת"כ, דכתיב: "[וכל] כלי חרס", לרבות כלי נתר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:1:1.english: “They should not become impure from their outer side. Why, then, did we learn: Natron vessels and earthenware vessels, etc.” - And the Rashba raises a difficulty: For [the Gemara] should have cited the baraita of the Tosefta of Kelim: “A needle, a ring, the base of a wooden vessel, glass vessels, and bone vessels — one may not draw [water] with them, and one may not sanctify [the ashes] with them, and they do not protect [from impurity in a corpse-tent] with a tightly sealed lid [tzamid patil]” — which shows that they become impure from their outer side! And why did [the Gemara] cite this [mishna], from which it could only prove [its point] by means of an inference: “It is natron vessels and earthenware vessels whose impurity is equal, etc.”? And furthermore, regarding this [mishna] that it cited, one could say that it only counted natron vessels and earthenware vessels because they are [susceptible to impurity] by Torah law — for [the impurity of] natron vessels is derived by us in Torat Kohanim, as it is written: “[And every] earthenware vessel” (Leviticus 11:33), to include natron vessels.

Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:1:2.hebrew: ה"ג רש"י מיטמאין ומטמאין מאויריהן ומיטמאין מאחוריהן ואין מיטמאין מגביהן - ופירש דמיטמאין מאחוריהן במקום חקק בית מושבן, כל שכן דמטמאין אחרים, כדמוכח בפ' העור והרוטב (חולין דף קיח.): "מרובה מדת לטמא ממדת ליטמא", דהשתא עיולי עיילא, אפוקי מיבעיא?! והא דלא קתני "מטמאין ומיטמאין מאחוריהן" כדתנן גבי אויריהן — משום דגבי אויריהן יש חידוש משניהם, מה שאין כן בכלים אחרים, שאינם מטמאין ולא מיטמאין מאויר; אבל במה שמטמא אחרים מאחוריו אין זה חידוש, דאפילו מגבן נמי מטמאין אחרים, וכן כל הכלים, וכ"ש אלו מאחוריהן דאיכא חקק; אבל "מיטמאין מאחוריהן" תנא לאשמעינן, דאע"ג דאין מיטמאין מגבן, אפילו הכי מיטמאין מאחוריהן. ולהכי לא עריב להו: "מטמאין ומיטמאין מאויריהם ומאחוריהן" — משום דבאויריהן הוי חידוש משניהם, אבל באחוריהם אין חידוש אלא במיטמאין לחוד. א"נ: מטמאין מאויריהן היינו דאוריי', אבל מאחוריהן לא הוי אלא מדרבנן. ועוד: דמיטמאין מאויריהן היינו כל הכלי, אבל מיטמאין מאחוריהן מצי למימר שאין מיטמא אלא גבו לבד. והא דתניא בת"כ: "מרובה מדת לטמא מליטמא, שמטמא אחרים מאחוריו ואין מיטמא מאחוריו" — מצינו למימר דאחוריו דקאמר התם היינו גב, ולא חקק בית מושב. א"נ: אינו מיטמא מאחוריו מדאוריי', אבל מדרבנן מיטמא. א"נ: אפי' מדאוריי' מיטמא מאחוריו, והא דקאמר "אינו מיטמא מאחוריו" היינו כולו, דאינו טמא כשקבל טומאה מאחוריו אלא גבו, אבל תוכו לא. והשתא אתי שפיר הא דאמרי' בפ' אלו מומין (בכורות דף לח. ושם): "כלי חרס נטמא גבו לא נטמא תוכו", משמע דגבו מיהא טמא; והיינו כי נטמא מאחוריו במקום חקק, וקרי ליה זימנין גבו וזמנין אחוריו. ומה שכלי חרס מציל — היינו אפילו ביש לו חקק, שאם נטמא גבו, תוכו טהור גמור. והא דתניא בתוספתא דכלים: "כלי חרס אין לו טומאה אלא מאוירו והיסטו" — לא אתי למעוטי אחוריו, אלא גבו; וחקק הוי בכלל אוירא. והקשה ה"ר אליעזר הזקן ז"ל לפ"ה: דתניא בתוספתא דכלים: "זה הכלל: כל המשמש כפוי בכלי חרס טהור", ואחורים הן משתמשין כפויים! ותירץ רבינו שמואל: דהתם בכיסוי קדרה ואלפס, דאיירי בהם התם לעיל, כמו שמפורש הטעם בת"כ: "יכול שאני מרבה אף חפוי הכלי? ת"ל: 'אשר יעשה מלאכה בהם' — פרט לכיסוי הכלי שאין עושין בהן מלאכה"; אבל אחורים — פעמים שכופין פניהם למטה, ועושין בהן מלאכה בתוך אחורים. ור"י מפרש דגרסי' הכי: "מטמאין מאחוריהם" — פירוש: מאויר אחוריהן, אם קבלו טומאה מתוכן; "ואין מיטמאין מגבן" — פירוש: לא מקבלי טומאה אפילו בנגיעת גבן, וכ"ש מאויר אחוריהן דאין מקבלין טומאה, וה"ה בנגיעת אחוריו נמי לא מקבלי טומאה. והא דלא נקט "דאין מיטמאין מאחוריהם" — משום דלא נטעי לומר דהיינו אויר אחוריהן, אבל בנגיעת אחוריהן טמא, להכי נקטו "ואין מיטמאין מגבן", דאין כאן אלא נגיעה. והא דלא עריב ותני להו: "מטמאין ואין מיטמאין מאחוריהן ומגביהן" — היינו משום שלא הוי מפרש רבותא בגביהן ורבותא באחוריהם; אבל השתא תנן: "מטמאין מאחוריהן" לרבותא, דאפי' באויר אחוריהן מטמאין, "ואין מיטמא מגבן", דאפי' בנגיעה לא מקבלין טומאה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:1:2.english: This is the version of Rashi: “They become impure and render [other items] impure from their airspace, and they become impure from behind, and they do not become impure from their outer side” - And [Rashi] explained that “they become impure from behind” [means] at the place of the indentation of their base. All the more so do they render other [items] impure [from behind], as is demonstrated in the chapter [entitled] Ha’or Veharotev (Chullin 118a): “The measure of rendering [others] impure is greater than the measure of becoming impure” — for now, [if impurity] enters [into the vessel through this hollow, it becomes impure]; is it necessary [to state that the vessel can] impart [impurity to other items placed there]?! And that which [the mishna] did not teach: “they render [others] impure and become impure from behind,” as it taught regarding their airspace — [this is] because regarding their airspace, there is a novel ruling in both of them, which is not the case for other vessels, which neither render [others] impure nor become impure from [their] airspace; but in rendering other [items] impure from its behind there is no novelty, for even from their outer side [earthenware vessels] also render other [items] impure, and so too all vessels, and all the more so these [earthenware and natron vessels] from behind, where there is an indentation. But “they become impure from behind” [the Tanna] taught to inform us that even though they do not become impure from their outer side, even so they become impure from behind. And for this reason [the Tanna] did not combine them [to teach]: “they render [others] impure and become impure from their airspace and from behind” — because in their airspace it is a novel ruling in both of them, but in their behind there is a novelty only with regard to becoming impure alone. Alternatively: rendering [others] impure from their airspace is by Torah law, but from behind it is only rabbinic. And furthermore: “they become impure from their airspace” means the entire vessel [becomes impure], but “they become impure from behind,” one can say that only its outer side becomes impure [while its interior remains pure]. And that which is taught in Torat Kohanim: “The measure of rendering [others] impure is greater than the measure of becoming impure, for it renders other [items] impure from behind, but does not become impure from behind” — we can say that “its behind” stated there means the [sloped] outer side, and not the indentation of the base. Alternatively: it does not become impure from behind by Torah law, but by rabbinic law it does become impure. Alternatively: even by Torah law it becomes impure from behind, and that which it says: “it does not become impure from behind” means its entirety [does not become impure], for when it received impurity from behind, only its outer side is impure, but its interior is not. And now that which we say in the chapter [entitled] Elu Mumin (Bekhorot 38a, and there): “[If] an earthenware vessel had its outer side become impure, its interior did not become impure” is well understood — which implies that at any rate its outer side is impure; and this is when it became impure from behind at the place of the indentation, and [the Gemara] calls it sometimes “its outer side” and sometimes “its behind.” And that which an earthenware vessel protects [its contents in an impure tent] is even when it has an indentation, for if its outer side became impure, its interior is completely pure. And that which is taught in the Tosefta of Kelim: “An earthenware vessel has impurity only from its airspace and its movement” — it did not come to exclude its behind, but rather its [plain] outer side, and an indentation is included in [the category of] airspace. And Rabbi Eliezer the Elder, of blessed memory, raised a difficulty against Rashi’s explanation: For it is taught in the Tosefta of Kelim: “This is the general rule: Anything in an earthenware vessel that is used upside-down is pure” — and the behind is used upside-down! And Rabbeinu Shmuel answered: There [in the Tosefta, it is referring to] the lid of a pot and an ilpas [stew-pot], which [the Tosefta] is discussing there earlier, as the reason is explained in Torat Kohanim: “Could it be that I include even the covering of the vessel? The verse states: ‘That work is done with them’ (Leviticus 11:32) — excluding the cover of a vessel, with which work is not done.” But the behind — sometimes they turn its face downward and do work inside the behind. And the Ri explains that we read [the text] this way: “They render [others] impure from their behind” — explanation: from the airspace of their behind, if they received impurity from their inside; “and they do not become impure from their outer side” — explanation: they do not receive impurity even by contact with their outer side, and all the more so from the airspace of their behind they do not receive impurity; and the same applies to contact with their behind, they also do not receive impurity. And that which [the Tanna] did not formulate: “and they do not become impure from their behind” is so that we would not mistakenly say that this [applies only to] the airspace of their behind, but by contact with their behind it is impure; for this reason they formulated: “and they do not become impure from their outer side,” for here there is only contact. And that which [the Tanna] did not combine and teach them [together]: “they render [others] impure and do not become impure from their behind and from their outer side” — that was because it would not have clarified the novel point in their outer side and the novel point in their behind. But now, we learned: “they render [others] impure from their behind” as a novel point, that even in the airspace of their behind they render [others] impure; “and it does not become impure from its outer side,” that even by contact they do not receive impurity.

Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:1:3.hebrew: אלא כיון דכי נשברו יש להם תקנה - ל"ג "אלא", דלא הדר ביה ממאי דאמר "שוינהו רבנן ככלי חרס"; דמשום טעם דנשברו יש להם תקנה אין סברא להוריד להם טומאה, אלא משום דלכלי חרס דמי לגמרי. וכיון דכבר הורידו להם טומאה משום דדמו לכלי חרס — משום כיון דנשברו יש להם תקנה, שוינהו רבנן כמתכות לענין טומאת גבן:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:1:3.english: "Rather, since if they broke they have a remedy" - We do not read "Rather" [ela], for [the Gemara] does not retract what it stated [previously]: "The Rabbis equated them to earthenware vessels"; for based on the reason that "if they broke they have a remedy," there is no logical basis to impose ritual impurity upon them; rather, [impurity was imposed] because they are completely similar to earthenware vessels. And once they already imposed ritual impurity upon them because they resemble earthenware vessels — on account of [the fact that] "since if they broke they have a remedy," the Rabbis equated them to metal vessels regarding the impurity of their outer side.

Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:3:1.hebrew: בטומאה דרבנן לא אחיתו לה רבנן טומאה - וקשה לר"י, דאמר במס' ע"ז פ' ר' ישמעאל (עבודה זרה דף נב. ושם): "ריתך כלי לע"ז — מהו?" — אמר: רב המנונא טומאה ישנה קמיבעיא להו, דתנן: "חזר ועשה מהן כלים — חזרו לטומאתן ישנה"; אלמא אפילו בטומאה דרבנן נמי איכא טומאה ישנה! ויש לומר: אע"פ דאמר התם בטומאה דרבנן היא, מ"מ הכלי מקבל טומאה מדאורייתא; אבל הכא, כלי זכוכית, דלא מקבל שום טומאה מדאורייתא אלא מדרבנן — פשיטא ליה דלא אחיתו להו רבנן טומאה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:3:1.english: “With regard to impurity by rabbinic law, the Sages did not impose impurity upon it” - And the Ri raises a difficulty: For [the Gemara] says in tractate Avodah Zarah, chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Avodah Zarah 52a, and there): “[If] one welded a vessel for idol worship, what is [the halakha]?” — [and the Gemara] said: Rav Hamnuna was raising a dilemma with regard to previous impurity, as we learned: “If he remade them into vessels, they returned to their previous impurity.” This implies that even in [the case of] rabbinic impurity there is also previous impurity! And one can say: Even though [the Gemara] said there that it is rabbinic impurity, nevertheless the vessel is susceptible to impurity by Torah law; but here, [in the case of] a glass vessel, which is not susceptible to any impurity by Torah law but only by rabbinic law, it is obvious to [the Gemara] that the Sages did not impose [previous] impurity upon them.

Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:4:1.hebrew: עבדי רבנן היכרא דלא לישרוף תרומה וקדשים - במאי דאין חוזרין לטומאה ישנה, לא הוי היכרא; דהא כלי מתכות נמי אין חוזרין לטומאה ישנה אלא מדרבנן, וליכא היכרא דאורייתא. וקשה לר"י: דילמא לעולם לכלי חרס דמו, דאין מטמאין מגבן; והאי דלא תני ליה בהדי כלי נתר וכלי חרס — משום דהנהו מיטמאין באויר, אבל כלי זכוכית לא מיטמא מאויר, דעבדו רבנן היכרא דלא נישרוף וכו' — דכה"ג אמר בפרק במה טומנין (לקמן שבת דף מח:) דבית הפך ובית התבלין ר' מאיר מטמא במגע אבל לא באויר, דעביד רבנן היכרא? ותי' ר"י הבחור: דע"כ כלי זכוכית מטמו מגבן — מתוספתא דכלים שהבאתי לעיל, שאין מצילין בצמיד פתיל. ולמאי דפרישית נמי לעיל, דדווקא אטומאת גב לא שורפין, שאין טמא אלא משום דדמי לכלי מתכות, אבל ממה שמטמא מתורת כלי חרס שורפין — אתי נמי שפיר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 16a:4:1.english: The Sages made a distinction in order not to burn terumah and consecrated items - The fact that [glass vessels] do not revert to their old impurity would not constitute a [sufficient] distinction, for metal vessels also revert to their old impurity only by rabbinic decree, and [thus] there would be no distinction [regarding an impurity that is] by Torah law. And Ri raises a difficulty: Perhaps [glass vessels] are actually comparable to earthenware vessels, in that they do not contract impurity from their back; and as for the fact that [the Mishnah] did not teach it together with natron vessels and earthenware vessels, [that is] because those contract impurity through their airspace, whereas a glass vessel does not contract impurity through its airspace, for the Sages made a distinction so that they would not burn [terumah and consecrated items], etc. — as [the Gemara] says in a similar manner in the chapter [entitled] Bameh Tomnin (below, Shabbat 48b) that [regarding] the cruse-receptacle and the spice-receptacle, Rabbi Meir deems [them] impure through contact, but not through airspace, because the Sages made a distinction? And Ri HaBachur answered that, perforce, glass vessels contract impurity from their back — from the Tosefta in Kelim that I cited above, [which teaches] that they do not protect with a tightly sealed cover. And according to what I also explained above — that specifically for impurity of the back they do not burn [terumah], since it is impure only because they equated it to metal vessels, but for that which contracts impurity under the category of earthenware vessels they [do] burn [terumah] — [this] also works out well.
